thread:
Alex Chen: Quick Q — we shipped the demo booth to Madrid for KubeCon and the customs broker invoiced VAT + a brokerage fee. Do I just upload the broker invoice to Expensely or is there more (commercial invoice, packing list, proof of payment)? Also curious if the person who stayed with the shipment that night can claim per-diem for meals.
Maria (People Ops): Short answer: yes you need more docs. 
Maria (People Ops): Please attach the commercial invoice, broker invoice, proof of payment (bank/cc), and the packing list. If Redwood is the owner of the shipped items, customs/duties are eligible for reimbursement if pre-approved.
Alex Chen: Got it, thanks. Is pre-approval retroactive possible? We didn't expect a broker fee that big. :grimacing:
Sam Patel (Finance): Retro pre-approval is not guaranteed. If you didn't get prior sign-off, escalate with receipts + a note from your manager explaining why it was unavoidable. We'll review case-by-case. :memo:
Sam Patel (Finance): For VAT specifically — if the broker/vendor provides a VAT invoice showing VAT separately and our VAT/Tax ID is on the invoice, AP can process reclaim. Otherwise VAT is usually non-reclaimable and treated as a reimbursable expense.
Jules Arora (Events): Adding event context — this was company-owned booth hardware, not personal. We had an on-site person (Tess) who stayed overnight to receive customs clearance. Can Tess claim per-diem?
Maria (People Ops): Per policy: per-diem applies for overnight travel on company business. If Tess stayed overnight due to shipment handling and it was an approved overnight, she can claim per-diem for that night. If she just did a same-day delivery, no per-diem.
Alex Chen: Perfect. Any specifics for how to label the expense so finance codes it to events budget?
Sam Patel (Finance): Use these fields in Expensely (copy/paste):
```
Expense type: "Customs & Brokerage"
Project/Cost center: "Events - KubeCon"
GL account: "6020 - Events & Shows"
Description: "Demo booth (Redwood property) - customs broker fee + VAT (if applicable)"
Required attachments: commercial_invoice.pdf, broker_invoice.pdf, proof_of_payment.pdf, packing_list.pdf, travel_auth.pdf
```
Sam Patel (Finance): If any docs are in Spanish, upload originals + an English summary. AP may ask for original signed commercial invoice for reclaim. Processing timeline for reclaimable VAT is typically 60–90 days.
Alex Chen: Who do we CC if we need AP help with VAT reclaim forms?
Sam Patel (Finance): Email ap@redwood.com and put events@redwood.com on cc. If you want finance to open the reclaim, include the scanned originals and the broker's VAT invoice.
Jules Arora (Events): Logistics note — keep photos of the shipment condition on arrival and the carrier's manifest. That helps with customs queries. :camera_flash:
Maria (People Ops): Also: if brokerage fees were charged due to missing export documentation from our side, we may not cover them without manager justification. Keep packing lists and export docs in the expense.
expense-bot: Reminder: attach all receipts as one PDF or multiple files under 10MB each. For multi-line claims, submit a single expense with multiple attachments.
Alex Chen: Thanks all — I'll gather docs and submit. If finance needs anything else I'll ping here. :thumbsup:
